Commentary.Commentary: Yasir Shah picked up two wickets in as many deliveries to get rid of de Grandhomme and Watling, as both were looking for the quick runs, but it came a little too late. By then, the Black Caps had more or less ran away with the game. Pakistan are going to now have to bat out of their skins to even save this Test, let alone win it. The surface isn't exactly naughty, but Pakistan and their fourth innings jitters could be a cause for worry. Don't go anywhere, the final innings will begin shortly.

So Williamson signals his players to come back in. The declaration is made and New Zealand have set a target of 280 in front of Pakistan. Good call from the Kiwi skipper, the intent is clear that he wants to give his team the best possible chance to win this Test. He's probably declared earlier than what he originally thought, and that's been aided by Colin de Grandhomme. After Kane was dismissed by Hasan Ali on the first ball of the day, Colin came in and just started swinging his bat. He added 62 runs in 39 balls with Henry Nicholls (who scored a ton) and propelled New Zealand to a commanding position in no time.

An appeal follows and the umpire, after giving it a thought, raises his finger. Kane walks up to his partner and then signals the 'T'. Time for the replays and it shows the on-field decision is the right one.

The last day of this series decider is set up to be a good one. All three results are very much possible. New Zealand have a lead of 198, courtesy Kane Williamson and Henry Nicholls' double hundred stand. They're going to want to get close to 250, possibly even more, but as quick as possible, so as to give themselves a chance to win this game and the series. Rarely does it happen that Pakistan enter the final day of a Test match in the U.A.E. as second favourites. A draw seems like the best possible result for the home side. What will happen? Will the Black Caps be satisfied with a draw? Will they go for the kill and try to run over Pakistan? Will the hosts manage a draw if that situation arises? Nobody can really tell. We'll find out soon enough.

So, as things stand, the Black Caps have ensured, or at least minimized the possibility of Pakistan winning this Test match. A result either way, or a draw as well, are possible. Pakistan looked toothless in attack on the whole. Yasir Shah and Shaheen Afridi got a wicket apiece to get things going, but since have been quite playable. Bilal Asif too, who couldn't provide anything different. Some fingers might be pointed towards Sarfraz Ahmed's captaincy, as he just seemed to run out of ideas after a point and didn't try anything different to spark some motivation from somewhere. Hasan Ali isn't a 100 percent either, so that could be the reason why Pakistan never took the new ball.

New Zealand's day hands down. This day hasn't gone as anyone thought. Everyone was expecting Pakistan to run through New Zealand, but Kane Williamson and Henry Nicholls have held the fort down and provided stern resistance to defy all odds. The Kiwi skipper scored a fine ton, and had ample support in Nicholls who crafted a fine fifty of his own, and the duo went on to add 212 runs for the 5th wicket, remaining unbeaten at the end of day's play. A lot of credit should go to Williamson. After his side lost a couple of wickets early in the day, he kept his calm, mixed attack and defense well and brought up his 19th Test ton.

One would believe that now the Black Caps are slightly in the driver's seat and they might start being even more aggressive in the next session. As for the hosts, they have to hope for a massive collapse so that the target can be stopped to an achievable one in the fourth innings. With the ghosts of the first Test still fresh in their memory, Pakistan would be vary about chasing anything more than 170-180. Can they come back after Tea and pick up some quick wickets? Join us in a bit for the last session.

What a magnificent session it has been for the visitors. 29 overs, 87 runs and no wicket lost. Almost game-changing one could say. Terrific knock from the New Zealand skipper, Kane Williamson and his partner Henry Nicholls. Their partnership is unbeaten and worth 139 at the moment. The lead has swelled to 125 and the whole momentum of the game has changed. Every question asked by the Pakistani bowlers has been answered with aplomb. Lots of tiring faces and dropping shoulders.
Drifts on the pads, Nicholls comfortably flicks it towards square leg for a single. That's the end of this session and the players will walk in for TEA.
Tossed up on the off stump and Nicholls blocks it away off his front foot.
A bit shorter in length this time by Hafeez, Williamson pushes it on his back foot towards the fielder at long on for a single.
Tossed up outside off Williamson blocks it off his front foot.
Once again drifts on to the pads of Williamson who tries to flick it but the ball misses and hits his pad.
Drifts on the legs, Nicholls flicks it away on the leg side towards the square leg fielder for a single.
Mohammad Hafeez to roll his arm over. Should most probably be the last over before Tea.
Tossed up again on off, Williamson rocks back and cuts it to point.
Flighted delivery on off, Williamson defends off the front foot.
Floated on leg, the left-hander flicks it towards the leg side for a single.
Tossed up on leg, Nicholls pushes it to the leg side off his pads.
Tossed up on middle, Nicholls defends off the front foot.
Short outside off, Williamson slaps it towards covers for a single.
Azhar Ali has been called to roll his arm over.
Floated on middle, Nicholls defends from within the crease.
Tossed up on leg, the southpaw pushes it to the leg side.
Flighted delivery on middle, the left-hander flicks it to mid-wicket.
Tossed up on leg, Nicholls blocks it well.
Good bowling by Yasir Shah. Tossed up on middle, Williamson rocks back and cuts it towards point for a single.
Tossed up on leg, Nicholls flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Another dot ball to end the over. New Zealand looking really solid here. Lots of dropping shoulders among the fielding team.
A length delivery just outside off, Williamson defends it staying inside the crease.
Another short of a length delivery and pushed straight back with good timing but no run.
Punched straight to the cover fielder off the back foot.
Good length ball on off, he drives it towards mid off.

FOUR! Test match century no. 19 for King Kane! His first of this series but could just be the most important one. Short and outside off, the skipper rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The ball races to the boundary. Well played and at such a crucial juncture! The first hundred by a Kiwi on this tour too. Might just turn out to be match-winning.
Tossed up on middle, Nicholls blocks it well.
Flighted delivery on middle, Nicholls tucks it to mid-wicket.
Floated on off, the southpaw defends off the back foot.
Tossed up on middle, the left-hander defends off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on off, Nicholls hits it straight towards the bowler.
Short on off, Nicholls drives it to covers.
Full this time outside off, Williamson pushes it towards the fielder at mid off.
Length delivery outside off, Williamson pushes it towards the point.
Fuller this time and the skipper defends it off his front foot.
Good length delivery outside off, Williamson tries to defend it but the ball keeps low and misses his bat and goes to the keeper on the bounce.

FOUR! Classic Williamson! Hasan Ali pitches it on good length outside off no movement for the bowler there, Williamson is well settled and drives it through covers for a boundary. He is just 2 short of another brilliant and well deserved century.
Good length outside off from Hasan, Williamson blocks it away.
Hasan Ali back on for another spell.
Watchfully kept out by Nicholls on this occasion. 6 runs off the over.

DROPPED! Another one goes down! This was tough but no excuses. Flatter ball at the pads, Henry goes for the flick but gets the inner half. Imam dives to his left and the ball was always going away, but he gets his hand to it and should have held on. Frustration for Pakistan.
Flatter and at the pads, Williamson works it towards fine leg for a run.

Down the wicket again and pushed down to long on. That's the fifty for Nicholls! Brilliant innings and what a time to play it. 8th Test fifty and it is helping New Zealand get into a strong position here.
FOUR! The runs are flowing here now! Flighted generously, Henry is down the track seeing this and lifts it over mid on for a four. The ball just lands inside the fence. Moves to 49.
This one is flighted on middle, HN comes forward and defends it well.
Tossed up on leg, Williamson pushes it to the leg side.
Flighted delivery on leg, Nicholls looks to defend but gets an outside edge past slip. The batsmen take a run.
Beautiful delivery from Bilal Asif. Turns into off, Nicholls looks to cut but gets beaten on this one. It missed the off stump by a whisker. Nothing going Pakistan's way.
Tossed up on middle, the left-hander defends off the back foot.
Flighted delivery outside off, Nicholls lets it go.
Tossed up on off, Nicholls defends off the front foot.

The ball does too much again and it beats everyone, including the keeper. Landing outside off and turns a mile to beat the batsman as he tries to work it on the leg side and the keeper who is blinded while going to collect it. The ball runs away fine but is stopped inside the fence. The batsmen come back for three. Valuable runs, all of these.
Another flat delivery outside off that turns into Henry. He flicks it away on the leg side towards square leg and picks up a couple of runs. The lead is 100 now.
Pitches this well outside off and the ball spins a long way in. Nicholls tries to flick it but misses and gets hit on the pad. The ball was doing too much and hence no appeal.
Flatter ball outside off, Henry is well ahead as he keeps it out.
Flighted ball outside off, Nicholls prods ahead and defends it into the ground.
Around the wicket, Kane pushes it to the vacant mid-wicket area for a single.
Floated on off, the left-hander defends off the front foot.
Tossed up on off, Nicholls keeps it out.
Flighted delivery outside off, Nicholls lets it go.
Short on off, Williamson rocks back and slaps it through covers. The fielder chases it and the batsmen get three runs. Williamson moves into the 90s.
Flighted delivery on off, Williamson defends off the front foot.
Tossed up on off, Williamson pushes it to short mid-wicket.
Flighted delivery outside off, Nicholls blocks it away.
No sharp turn here for Yasir, Nicholls defends it off his back foot.
Once again tosses it up outside off, Nicholls has no problem keeping that away.
Tossed up outside off, Nicholls sweeps it away towards the short fine leg fielder.
Fuller this time and Nicholls blocks it off his front foot.
Shorter on length outside off Nicholls pushes it off his back foot
A big stride ahead to this loopy one on middle and pushed to short mid-wicket by the skipper.
Williamson remains in his crease and defends this.
Flatter delivery on middle, Kane shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Just dropped this one onto the leg side and runs through for a single.
Flatter delivery on off and middle, Nicholls flicks it towards the square leg fielder.
Looped up outside off, Kane pushes it towards mid-wicket for a run and gets to the other end.
FOUR! Good shot. Floated on middle, Nicholls sweeps it towards fine leg for a boundary.
Flighted delivery on off, Nicholls looks to defend but gets hit on the pads.
Tossed up on leg, the batsman pushes it to the leg side.

APPEAL FOR LBW! NOT OUT! Turns in sharply, Nicholls looks to defend but gets hit on the back pad. The bowler appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Pakistan don't have any review. Replays show that impact was outside off.
Flighted delivery on middle, Williamson plays it with soft hands towards third man for a single.
Tossed up outside off, Nicholls sweeps it towards fine leg for a single.
Yasir Shah is called on to bowl again.

FOUR! What a shot! Timing at its best. Flighted delivery on middle, Kane dances down the track and just pushes this one through the gap on the leg side for four towards the mid-wicket fence. Such beautiful usage of the wrists here. The ball is timed so well that even on this slow outfield it reaches the fence with just a push. The 100-run stand also comes up between these two with this shot.
Another drop down by the NZ skipper towards fine leg but no run available this time.
Nicholls nudges this one onto the leg side towards mid-wicket and picks up one.
Shorter delivery at the pads, Kane works it behind square leg and gets to the other end. The partnership is worth 95 now.

DROPPED! Short and on middle, Williamson rocks back and pulls it away hard but in the air! Yasir at square leg seems to have lost the ball and reacts pretty late and cannot hold on to it. Was a regulation catch, should've been taken. How much will this go on to affect the hosts? The batsmen come back for a couple as the ball rolls to deep square leg.
Around the wicket to the skipper, he calmly pats it away to short mid-wicket.

Drinks break. New Zealand are slowly draining the life out of the Pakistani bowlers and along with it, taking this Test match away from them too. Solid stuff from the NZ skipper and Henry Nicholls. Since Lunch, there hasn't been an occasion where they looked really troubled. Pakistan need to do something here and in quick time.
Once again short by Shaheen, this time its quicker and Nicholls ducks underneath it.
Short by Afridi, Nicholls gets on his back foot ad plays the pull shot towards the fine leg region. They take a comfortable two by the time the ball is thrown back to the keeper.

Full and outside off once again by Afridi, Nicholls tries to defend it off his front foot but the ball finds the outside edge and move towards the third man region. The batsmen take 2 runs. This brings up 150 for New Zealand and extends their lead to 76. These two would like to continue their partnership and put on a good total for Pakistan to chase.
Fuller this time by Shahen, Nicholls gets behind it and defends it off his front foot.
Length delivery on off defended well by Nicholls.
Good length ball on top of off stump, Nicholls defends it back to the bowler.
Dot ball to end the over, Kane defends it onto the leg side with such soft hands again. Good over after the boundary on the first ball.
This one bounces a bit more but Williamson adjusts well and defends it into the ground with soft hands.
Another ball on and around off, KW is solid in defense though.
Much better from Asif, the skipper comes half forward and dead bats it.
Flatter ball at the pads and Williamson defends it watchfully.

FOUR! Williamson goes on his back foot and punches it towards the cover region for a boundary. Brilliant shot which was timed to perfection by the Kiwi skipper to move to 80. A very bad delivery by Bilal. If you give Williamson this much time and width he will punish you everyday.
A good 3 balls after being hit for the boundary. This one is on off stump and slightly coming in after landing. Nicholls deals with it easily though.
Another ball outside off that is let go through to the keeper.
Pitched fuller and outside off, left alone this time.
FOUR! Wide, very wide. And it gets the treatment it deserves. Henry cuts it beautifully behind point and to the fence for four. Such important runs for the visitors these.
This one is attacking off stump, Nicholls comes half ahead to defend into the pitch.
Good length ball that reverses in after landing. Nicholls goes for the flick but gets an inside edge onto the thigh pad.
Loopy delivery on middle, the skipper defends off the back foot.
Floated on off, Williamson keeps it out.
Flighted delivery on middle, Williamson defends off the back foot.
Extra bounce on this one. The captain pushes it past short leg.
Tossed up again on off, the skipper opens the face of the bat and hits it towards point. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Tossed up on middle, Williamson blocks it well.
Williamson blocks it  off his back foot.
Length delivery outside off, the ball moves in after pitching and finds the inside edge of the skipper's bat.
Good length delivery once again but this time there is width for Williamson to push it off his back foot towards covers for a single.
Once again the ball is bowled on length delivery on off, Williamson blocks it off his back foot.
Pulls back his length this time and Williamson defends it off his back foot.

FOUR! Driven and driven beautifully by Williamson. Typical Williamson drive there. He looks so comfortable out there in the middle. The ball is overpitched outside off and the Kiwi skipper gets on his front foot and drives it superbly through covers.
Looped up outside off, Nicholls drives but short cover stops it with an outstretched left arm.
Flatter delivery on middle, HN comes ahead and defends this into the ground.
Outside off and the batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Grip and turn! Nicholls is ahead in defense but the ball turns enough to beat the outside edge. Lots of oohs and aahs around the bat.
Well outside off and straightens after landing, left alone by the batter.
Flighted outside off, overpitched. Nicholls jams it out towards cover.
Length delivery outside off, the ball jags back in and finds the inside edge of Williamson's defensive bat.
Outside off by Afridi, Williamson has no problem letting that one go.
Fuller this time and the Kiwi skipper beautifully drives it towards cover region but unfortunately for him the ball is straight to the fielder.
Length delivery once again. Williamson blocks it off his back foot.
Length delivery outside off driven towards the cover fielder by Williamson.
Afridi from over the wicket, bowls it on length on middle, Williamson blocks it off his front foot.
Shaheen Afridi has been called on to bowl. Can he break this partnership?
Floated again outside off, Nicholls lets it go.
Loopy delivery on off, the batsman blocks it well.
Floated on off, Nicholls defends off the front foot.
Flighted delivery on middle, the skipper drives it towards mid on for a single.
Full on middle, the skipper drives it straight back towards the bowler. Bilal Asif makes a diving stop.

Tossed up on middle, Williamson dances down the track and looks to hit over long on but does not get the distance. The skipper is beaten by the flight there but luckily the ball lands in no man's land. Azhar Ali chases from mid on but does not get there. The batsmen pick up a couple.

Short of a length this time by Hasan, Williamson punches it off his back foot towards extra cover. The ball is timed beautifully but doesn't have the legs behind it to go to the boundary. The batsman come back for the third.
Once again length delivery outside off, Williamson defends it confidently off his front foot.
Length delivery outside off, KW pushes it towards the cover region.
Length delivery on middle and off stump, Williamson nicely flicks it away towards the mid-wicket region for a couple. A run after 20 consecutive dot balls.
Length delivery on off, Williamson defends it off his front foot.
Short of a length on the off, the ball comes in and Williamson flicks it away towards the square leg fielder.
Floated outside off, Nicholls offers no shot. Third consecutive maiden over for Pakistan.
Tossed up on off, Nicholls defends off the front foot.
Loopy delivery outside off, the southpaw lets it go.
Flighted delivery outside off, the left-hander offers no shot.
Tossed up again outside off, Nicholls lets it go.
Tossed up on middle, Nicholls defends off the front foot.
A tad shorter this time on length delivery, Williamson keeps it away.
Hasan Ali is bowling a consistent line and length here but KW has easily defended it.
Length delivery outside off, KW defends off his front foot.
Once again a length delivery on off, Williamson pushes it towards the mid on region.
Length delivery outside off, the ball jags back and Williamson defends it off his front foot.
Length delivery outside off, Williamson drives it to mid off.
Floated outside off, the left-hander offers no shot.
Tossed up again on middle, the southpaw defends off the back foot.
Flighted delivery outside off, Nicholls shoulders his arms to this one.
Tossed up on off, Nicholls keeps it out.
Flighted delivery on middle, the batsman blocks it well.
Tossed up on off, Nicholls hits it to mid on.

FOUR! Adding insult to injury, one must say! Well outside off, Williamson gets in position and drives it beautifully through the gap on the offside for a boundary. The lead has gone above 50 with this four.

NOT OUT! The ball is missing leg and Pakistan have lost their second review. It was a big wicket and it seemed the hosts were very desperate to get him. The ball landed on middle and was going down with the angle. Williamson goes for the flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. A loud appeal but the umpire is unmoved. After a long discussion, the bowling team goes up for a review. There is no bat involved but the Ball-Tracker shows us that the ball is missing leg. Review lost and Williamson survives.
Review Time! Kane Williamson is rapped on the pad and the ball seems to be going down leg to the naked eye. The Pakistanis after a lot of deliberation, decide to go upstairs.

A little bit too straight on this occasion, beautifully worked away square of the wicket on the leg side. The batsmen can come back for three this time. Large boundaries but nevertheless, good running!
Was outside off again, this time Henry pokes at it. It takes a thick outside edge that runs away to the left of gully. The batsmen come back for another couple.
Well outside off and the ball holds its line after landing, the batsman lets it go.
Short of a length and angling into the body, Nicholls works it away in the gap through mid-wicket for a couple.
Flighted delivery on leg, the skipper flicks it to the leg side.

Tossed up on middle, Williamson dances down the track and hits it towards mid on. The skipper goes for the single and the fielder fires a throw at the non-striker's end. The throw is very wayward and it goes as overthrows towards third man. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Bowls down the leg side, Williamson lets it go.
Tossed up on middle, the skipper pushes it to the leg side.
Flighted delivery on middle, Williamson blocks it well.
Bowls down the leg side, Williamson lets it go.
Bilal Asif to bowl from the other end.
Maiden over to start off with. Slightly fuller ball outside off, the leftie is ahead in defense.
Similar delivery, Nicholls comes forward to defend but the ball takes the inside half of the bat and rolls down to square leg.
On a good length and top of off stump, the batsman is half-ahead as he defends again.
Another one, slightly more outside off. Nicholls is comfortable in defense.
Fuller and on off this time, Henry is well ahead in defense.
Around the wicket, short ball and sliding down leg with the angle. Nicholls misses the flick and gets hit on the hips.
The players are back onto the field for the 2nd session. Henry Nicholls to face the first ball after resumption. Hasan Ali to bowl.
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

Full marks to Pakistan. They bowled to a set plan and have been rewarded. They will believe that they are just a wicket away from enforcing a collapse but they need that dismissal soon. Anything close to 150 could be tricky on this surface, as we saw in the first Test. Join us back at 12.40 pm local (0840 GMT) for the second session.

Kane Williamson is the centre of the Kiwi batting wagonwheel. In the first innings, his 89 kept New Zealand afloat while in the second, he has kept Pakistan at bay. However, the Black Caps are not out of troubled waters yet, with the lead well under 50.

In reality, the Kiwis have lost only one quality wicket. The fact that Somerville hung around for 34 balls was not bad for them but Ross Taylor's wicket was a big blow. They were lucky that Nicholls survived an LBW call which would have been out had it been reviewed but that is how the game goes.
Absorbing session of cricket. 26 overs, 86 runs and 2 wickets. Could have been more but Pakistan will still take it.
Around off, spinning away, punched back defensively towards the bowler. LUNCH ON DAY 4, NEW ZEALAND LEAD BY 38!
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a run. Moves to 20.
Full and outside off, Kane reaches out to drive and gets it past short extra cover for a single.
Outside off, a touch short, punched straight to cover.
The googly, down the leg side, Kane misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
Full and outside off, Williamson looks to drive but misses.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
50-RUN STAND IS UP. Fine fightback from these two. Short and around off, Nicholls works it wide of mid on to bring up the 50-run stand.
Landed outside off, goes straight on, left alone.
EDGED, BUT SHORT! Nearly the fifth wicket. Full and outside off, Nicholls looks to push but the ball takes the outside edge and drops short of Asad Shafiq at first slip!
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, Kane dead-bats it.
Outside off, punched through mid on for a single.
On middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for three runs this time.
Outside off, played straight to point.

HALF CENTURY FOR WILLIAMSON! His 29th in Tests, 5th against Pakistan and third in the UAE. Nice knock to follow his 89 in the first dig. Around off, Williamson goes back and works it through mid-wicket for a couple. A solid knock. Can he get to a triple?
Short and outside off, punched uppishly, wide of the man at silly point, who turns away for cover. A single taken.
A short ball outside off, Williamson looks to pull but misses.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, Williamson drives it straight to short extra cover who fumbles and that results in three extra runs. 100 UP FOR NEW ZEALAND. Can they double this score? The lead is now 26.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

FOUR! Finally he connects! Nicholls has tried out umpteen reverse sweeps, only to mistime or miss so far. This time, he connects sweetly and gets it past short third man for a boundary. The lead is now 23.
Full and around off, watchfully pushed out.
On middle, flicked wide of mid on, towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! A real half tracker, barely bounces, but Williamson rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket. Hasan Ali puts in a dive again but fails once more. Gets up gingerly and limps. The stand is now worth 32.
Outside off, short in length, chopped straight to point.
Full and around off, spinning away, watchfully blocked out.
Floated outside off, driven straight to cover.
Around off, watchfully kept out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Bilal Asif returns. 4-0-8-0 so far.
FOUR.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Full and outside off, spinning away, Kane feels for it but misses as the ball turns a mile.
Gets the flick shot away this time, for a single through mid-wicket. Both, the lead and Nicholls, move to 10.

NOT OUT! MISSING LEG! Excellent review from New Zealand. That looked dead plumb. But Hawk Eye disagrees with Ian Gould. Full and outside off, Nicholls goes back to play that one but the ball spins in a mile off the rough and hits him in front of the stumps. Yasir appeals and Gould raises his finger. It does not take long for Williamson to nod his head in response to Nicholls' inquiring look for the review and sure enough - the decision is overturned!
Nicholls has been adjudged LBW! He has taken the review though.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Full and just outside off, well blocked out.
FOUR! That is a long hop, around middle. Williamson pulls it through mid-wicket and gets a boundary. The stand is now worth 23.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! IMPERIOUS! Slightly short from Yasir and Nicholls pounces. He rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.

Another shout for LBW, turned down again. Things continue to happen. This was much closer than the previous one. Full and outside off, spinning in, Nicholls looks to play the reverse sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. Impact was outside off on this occasion.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a couple. 'PAKISTAN WILL BAT AGAIN!' screams an excited Ramiz Raja on air.

Huge shout for LBW, no review taken. Probably doing too much. Full and outside off, Henry looks to play that from his crease but misses and is hit right in front of the stumps. That seemed to be going down leg. NO! HAWK EYE SHOWS IT TO BE HITTING LEG! If only had Pakistan  reviewed...
Full and outside off, Nicholls looks to play the reverse sweep but gets a bit of a bottom edge which rolls towards short third man.
Aha. The helmet is found. Both, the 12th and 13th men come out to give that ONE helmet. Azhar Ali goes under the lid at silly point.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

Interesting. A bit of a delay. Sarfraz wants someone under the lid. He has signalled towards the 12th man who, in turn, signals to the 13th man! Eventually, he too, disappears inside and the field is not changed.
Very full, around off, nicely blocked out.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
FOUR! Excellent shot! Fractionally short in length outside off, Williamson rocks back and cuts it through point for a boundary! Moves to 33 with his third boundary.
Full and around off, watchfully blocked out.

Huge shout for LBW! Turned down! Could be height, could be angle. On a length around off, nipping back in sharply, Williamson looked to defend but was beaten by pace and got hit on the pads. Hasan roared in an appeal, even extended it but umpire Reiffel patiently waited for all that to die down and then shook his head with a NO. Hawk Eye shows that to be clipping the top of leg stump, so the umpire's call would have stayed.
Double change. Hasan Ali finally gets a look-in after a solitary over this morning. 5-3-5-0 so far in this innings.
Full and around off, dead-batted nicely.
Spins in a long way from outside off, Nicholls gets across, then goes back and looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. Comfortably missing leg, hence no appeal.
Tossed up around off, spinning in, watchfully blocked out.
On middle and leg, flicked through square leg for a couple.
Full and around off, spinning in, watchfully defended.
On middle and leg, helped through mid-wicket for a single.
Yasir Shah is back on. Change of ends for him. 10-2-17-2 so far.
Full and around off, well defended.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Pushes this towards mid on, takes the fielder on and completes a quick single.
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Bilal Asif into the attack now. 3-0-7-0 so far.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full and around off, pushed towards cover.
One more leave outside off.
Outside off, left alone again.
Wide down the leg side, no trouble at all for the batsman.
Down the leg side, left alone.

DRINKS BREAK. What an entertaining hour of cricket. 13 overs, 2 wickets and 39 runs. Those runs came because of Taylor's counter-attack but otherwise Pakistan have been as frugal as they possibly could have been. The Kiwis are into the middle order now and only Williamson is their possible hope. Can they play around him and at least set a target of 100 for the home side?
Full and around off, well blocked out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.

THAT IS A GRUBBER! Holy me, Williamson is surely lucky to still be out there. Full and around off, the googly, Kane stays back to work it to the leg side but the ball shoots low and just about takes the bottom half of his bat, enroute short leg.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers where the fielder does well to stop it with a dive to his left.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
One more leave outside off.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, pretty full, just outside off, but left alone.

NOT OUT! The noise was of the bat hitting the back pad! Cannot blame Pakistan. On the first look, it seemed like there was a big edge. Full and outside off, Nicholls looked to drive but missed. There was a big noise and Sarfraz, along with the slip cordon, came charging towards the umpire in an appeal. But Ian Gould was as calm as a camel in a sandstorm. Did not panic at all. Shook his head and the skipper immediately went for the review. Sadly for him, Snickometer did not support his cause.
Howzzat? Howzzat? Howzzat? Pakistan are supremely confident that Nicholls has nicked one behind. He has not been given out though. The hosts take a review...
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
A bouncer, around middle, Williamson ducks.
Pitches this miles outside off and Nicholls still goes after it, only to pad it away. Misses.
On middle and leg, helped through mid-wicket for three runs.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
Around middle and off, well blocked out.
Comes down the track and watchfully blocks it out.
Full and around middle, chipped uppishly, but wide of the bowler towards mid on.
Outside off, left alone.
Henry Nicholls walks in at number 6, replacing Taylor.

OUT! Taylor has come and Taylor has gone! You live by the sword, so you die by it as well. Rosco's counter-attacking intent has not lasted long. A short ball, around middle, Ross has been looking to attack right from the time he arrived, so he does not bother to restrain himself. Goes after the pull but cannot quite keep it down. Gets a bit of a top edge which balloons in the air but hang on, where is Bilal Asif going? The ball is coming straight to him at deep square leg but he misjudges the catch. He comes running in but then goes back and has to adjust. Leaps and almost lets the ball slip out of his hands but thankfully for Pakistan, the ball sticks! Big wicket for the 'hosts.' Into the soft underbelly of a middle order now.
Outside off, good change of pace, Rosco looks to cut but misses.

FOUR! Terrific shot! Taylor is taking the bull by the horns. A short ball, around middle, Taylor swivels and pulls it behind square leg. There is a man in the deep, at square leg, but he cannot get there!
Around off, solidly defended.
On a length outside off, slanting away, Taylor pushes but misses.
The googly to end the over, Kane misses his defense and is hit on the pads. Pakistan straightaway appeal but that was missing leg.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Comes down the track and whips it wide of mid on for three. The deficit is now 19.
Outside off, punched off the back foot for a single.
Around off, blocked from the crease. 14 from the over!

FOUR! Oh ho ho! This is even better! Third boundary of the over and already tea pots are boiling in Sarfraz' face. On a length around off, angling away, Taylor waits for the ball to come to him and then opens the face of his bat to guide it past gully towards third man! 50 UP FOR NEW ZEALAND! They trail by 22 now.
FOUR! Counter-attacking, is he? Looks like we are gonna have fun. Full and outside off, Taylor reaches out this time and drives it between cover and mid off for the second boundary of the over!
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
FOUR! Much better from Taylor. Afridi overpitches on this occasion and this time Taylor makes good use of his feet. Gets close to the pitch of the ball and drives it past mid off.

UPPISH, BUT SAFE! A bit loose from Taylor. He needs to stitch a partnership here. Full and outside off, a touch wide, shaping away, Rosco plays away from his body and nearly spoons a catch to short extra cover. Luckily for him, it evades the fielder and the batsmen get a couple.
Comes out this time to block. Superb over from Yasir.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.

CLOSE CALL! Full and around off, Taylor dances down the track and pushes it towards mid on. Takes the fielder on and is in a bit of a strife but beats the throw as it misses the stumps at the bowler's end.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Ross Taylor walks in at number 5, replacing Somerville.

OUT! 200TH TEST WICKET FOR YASIR SHAH! The fastest ever to do so! Take a bow, maestro. In just 33 matches. Only the 7th Pakistan player to achieve this feat. Pitched around leg stump, Somerville looks to play that from the crease but misses and is hit right in front. A big appeal ensues and the umpire raises his finger! The night watchman has a bit of a chat with his skipper but not for long. Is sent back. Plumb in front.
Has Yasir got his 200th? Somerville has been adjudged plumb in front. He has taken a review though. Oh no, he hasn't. He was just walking across to his skipper for a chat. Is sent on his way.
A bouncer to end the over, Kane ducks.
Around off, solidly defended.

FOUR! SWEET! Kane Williamson at his best. Full and outside off, Williamson leans into the shot, uses the angle from the bowler and drives it through the covers for a boundary. Textbook shot. The deficit is now 37. The skipper moves to 22 with his second boundary and the stand is now worth 13.
On a length around middle and leg, angling away, pushed towards point.
Punches this off the back foot for a single.
Landed around off, shaping away, left alone.
Yes, they can. Full and around middle, watchfully pushed towards mid-wicket.
Sloppy from Pakistan. They have now allowed an easy single to Somerville. He just gets across and taps this to the on side, crossing over. Can they prevent Williamson from retaining the strike?
Outside off, punched back to the bowler.
Beauty. Full and around off, Will is drawn forward into the defense but the ball spins away past the outside edge.
Full and around off, Somerville stays back and defends.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for an easy single. That is a run given. Pakistan clearly want the night watchman facing as many balls as possible.
This is pitched outside leg, with the aim of moving the ball away, but Somerville defends it watchfully. Consecutive maidens for Afridi.
This time he watches the ball really closely and opens the face of the bat at the right time, pushing the ball to point.
Another play and a miss from the night watchman.
Beaten! This bloke is bowling really well. Lands this on the seam, around off, Will looks to defend but the late away movement squares him and beats the outside edge.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Ahh.... a play and a miss. Full and outside off, Somerville looks to drive but misses.
Ian Gould gets his scissors and takes some leather off the ball. Hey hey... we have a pacer from the other end! I thought it will be spin from both ends...
A bit of an issue with the ball.
Full and outside off, Will looks to flick but misses and gets a leading edge towards cover. A single taken.
A little bit of drift, coming into the batsman, Somerville gets across and defends.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Around middle, worked straight to short leg.
Looks to flick again but gets a bit of an inside edge onto his pads.
Full and down the leg side, Somerville misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
Straightaway a change. Just the one over for Hasan Ali this morning. Here comes Yasir Shah. One away from becoming the fastest to 200 Test wickets...
Around off again, watchfully defended from the crease.
Around off, angling away, punched towards cover.

Beauty. The length is a touch fuller and the skipper is beaten. Beautiful seam presentation, held upright, dangerous channel, around middle and leg, then getting it to seam away as KW feels for the ball.
A slower bouncer, around leg, Kane ducks.
Similar ball, once again a tight compact defense from the skipper.
On a length around off, watchfully punched back to the bowler.
Shaheen Afridi to bowl from the other end.
Once again Will stays back to defend and this time, does so properly.
Oohh... Somerville stays back to defend this but the ball stays a touch low, takes the inside edge and hits him on his pads.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to mid off.

Slightly wider outside off, which means Kane can free his arms a touch and punch it through then covers. First runs of the morning as the batsmen amble back for the third. Might have even run four, had they gone for it quickly.
Tighter line, closer to the off stump, Williamson defends stoutly.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
The players are slowly making their way out to the middle. It will be Hasan Ali to start the proceedings today to Kane Williamson. Here we go!

Will Somerville is having a chat with Danny Morrison. The spinner says that he is extremely excited to contribute to the team's cause. Hopes that he now does some bit with the bat too. On his childhood days, he says that he grew up in Wellington and watched Martin Crowe play cricket, who was his inspiration. Then adds further that he went to Australia to improve his cricket and then came back and played for Otago. On the current surface, Somerville says that it is a good surface but very difficult to score. Adds that patience is the key as wickets are not easy to come by either. Hopes that the wicket deteriorates from today which gives New Zealand the edge as they will be bowling last.

That was from New Zealand's point of view. Let us now see how Pakistan view it. A wicket early this morning - that of Kane Williamson - and we have a realistic chance of getting a holiday tomorrow. The pitch is turning square and Yasir and Bilal become threats again. Do not forget the Professor, Mohammad Hafeez.

When Azhar and Shafiq raised their double century stand, one felt that they have batted the Kiwis out of this Test match. Or set the platform to. But a collapse from 285/3 to 348 all out meant that this game has now turned into a one-inning shootout. The Black Caps have lost their openers already but they still have some decent batting to come. A target of around 200 would be more than a handful.

The great Matthew Hayden had once remarked - 'In  India, there could be hours of play where nothing seems to be happening. Then, all of a sudden, the Test match turns on its head.' Might as well change that part from India to Asia. For hours on Tuesday and Wednesday, it seemed like nothing is going to happen. And then suddenly, we are into a possibility of another quick finish. Hello and a warm welcome to the fourth day of the third Test between Pakistan and New Zealand in Abu Dhabi.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

48 more is what New Zealand trail by, they have their skipper out there and the tourists would hope, he bats long and the rest give him able support. Pakistan on the other hand, will want to bundle the visitors out quickly as anything above 150 could be a tricky chase with the wicket worsening. Will Pakistan continue their domination on Day 4 or will New Zealand fight back? Join us to find out at 1000 local (0600 GMT). Till then goodbye and take care.

They are in the driver's seat at the moment but could have been in an even better position had their middle and lower-order capitalized on the platform laid by Azhar Ali and Asad Shafiq. The duo, earlier in the day, stitched a mammoth 201-run stand, with both scoring a ton. Pakistan looked set to take a huge lead but Somerville weaved his magic and helped New Zealand fight back. However, wickets from Yasir Shah and Shaheen Afridi has once again seen them go on the back foot.

A session of two halves, the first hour was dominated by New Zealand and the second by Pakistan. But it is surely the hosts who walk off the field as the happier side. After their remaining 5 wickets fell for not a lot, they had around 14 overs to have a go at the Kiwi batsmen and they have managed to get rid of the two openers.
The last ball has been negotiated nicely! Floated up on off, Somerville meets it with the full face of the bat. STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Floats it up outside off, the batsman drives it to covers.
On the stumps again, another defensive shot on offer.
On the stumps, it is kept out.
Tosses it up on off, Somerville strokes it to mid off.
Flatter around off, Somerville goes back and defends it onto the ground.
Floated up on middle, it is kept out.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side. They pick up a single.

A huge appeal but not given! This is tossed up around middle, William lunges and tries to defend with bat and pad close. Not sure what it hit first. The Pakistan players appeal. The umpire shakes his head. Bilal really likes it but Sarfraz says it seems to be going down leg.
Down the leg side, Somerville misses the flick, the keeper too fails to collect but no runs taken.
Tosses it up outside off, William blocks it out.
Works it with the turn towards short fine leg and the batsmen take a run.
Pushes it into the same region to end the over.
Shorter and flatter outside off, forced away off the back foot to covers.
William Somerville is in as the nightwatchman.

OUT! Gone. That's actually a poor shot from Tom Latham. There isn't much time before end of day's play, should have been more cautious. Played right into Pakistan's hands really. Shah loops it up around off and it turns into the batsman, Latham gets low to sweep. Can't keep it down and it's straight towards Haris Sohail at deep square leg. He runs in, dives and takes a safe catch.
Coming in once more, Latham looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.

Loud shout for a leg before, turned down. The inside edge saves him there. Yasir comes from around the wicket and tosses it up outside off, it spins and catches Latham on the front pad. The appeal is denied though, as the ball first takes the inside edge. Good call from the umpire.
Short, spinning away from outside off, it's placed through the covers from the back foot for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
On the stumps and it is kept out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Williamson walks right across and flicks it to square leg for a run.
A little too full and outside off, the batter times it through covers for a run.
This is flatter and around off, pushed through covers for a run.
Tries to sweep but misses to get hit on the pads. An appeal follows but the umpire shakes his head. The impact was outside off.
Babar Azam is going to come in close to the batsman. He's called for a helmet and extra shin guards.
Tosses it up outside off, the ball pitches and turns back in. Latham tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tosses it up on off, the batter pushes it to covers.
This is flatter and outside off, Williamson cuts it to point.
This is stroked towards mid off for no runs.
On the stumps, it is kept out.
Just like that! The edge was induced but away from the first slip fielder. Floats it up on off, pitches and turns away. Latham tries to defend but gets an outside edge towards third man for a brace.
A little more straighter this time, this is outside off, it is left alone.
Nice! This is what he should be bowling. Loopy and lands it around off, it pitches and then turns away. Latham, however, keeps it out nicely.
Flatter again on off, Latham is solid in defense.
The slider on middle, Latham goes back and pushes it to mid-wicket.
Bilal Asif is into the attack now.
The batsman drives this through the covers.
Floats it up on off, the batsman is solid in defense.
Latham works it with the turn through mid-wicket for a run.
It is slightly on the shorter side, it is slapped through covers for a run.
Brings out the paddle sweep towards fine leg for a single.
Flatter and around off, the batsman is solid in defense.
Yasir Shah is into the attack.
A little too straight by Hasan, Latham tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. It goes towards fine leg. A leg bye is taken.
Attacks the off pole, the batsman gets right behind the line and defends it onto the ground.
On a length again and it is kept out nicely.
Fuller and around off, Williamson strokes it towards wide mid off for a run.
Good length around off, the ball stays a touch low. Williamson does well to keep it out.
Works it with the angle down to fine leg for a single.
Length delivery on off, the Kiwi skipper blocks it off his back foot.
Full outside off, Williamson defends it off his front foot.
Full on the middle stump and Latham punches it through the mid-wicket region. The fielder gives it a good chase and saves a run for his side. The batsman take three runs there.
Length delivery outside off, Williamson beautifully punches it off his back foot through cover-point for three runs.
Length again and Williamson shoulders arms to it.
Length delivery outside off, Williamson doesn't get in the way of the ball.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On the stumps, it is kept out.
The bumper on middle, the batsman ducks under it.
Back of a length around off, Latham goes back and keeps it out. Hasan is not getting the same amount of movement like Afridi.
Very full this time on off, Latham does not get it through and finds the fielder at covers.
Good length on off, the batsman is solid in defense.
FOUR! Wide outside off, Kane goes fishing and gets a thick outside edge that goes wide of the slips and to the fence for a boundary. Williamson gets off the mark in streaky fashion.
A full ball outside off to welcome the NZ skipper, he defends it calmly to cover.

OUT! Jeet Raval will have to go. The ball lands outside off and jags in late after landing. The leftie can't adjust and gets rapped on the knee roll. The umpire raises his finger after thinking for a bit. Jeet consults his partner and goes for the review. The Snickometer shows that there is no bat involved and the Ball Tracker shows that the impact and stumps would have been umpire's call. The decision stays and New Zealand lose their first wicket. The review is retained though. Also, Kane Williamson walks in next to bat.
Review time! Raval has been given out LBW. He has gone for a review. Looks out to the naked eye.

Outside off and the ball jags in after landing. Raval decides to leave it but the ball comes in and hits his knee roll on the way to Sarfraz. The Pakistanis appeal but the impact was outside off. Raval needs to be more careful with the ball swinging so much.
Just short of a good length outside off, Raval defends this from within the crease.
Short of a length and on middle, Raval pushes it to short mid-wicket.
Length delivery outside off, jags back in and once again finds the edge f Latham's bat who tries to block it away.
Length delivery outside off the ball moves back in and finds the inside edge of Latham's bat onto the pads. A few shouts for lbw but not a confident appeal.
Length delivery outside off, Raval leaves it alone.
What A beauty! Coming around the wicket, Ali bowls it a bit shorter and it jags back in. Misses the stumps.
Identical delivery, Jeet shoulders arms to it.
Length delivery on the stumps angles away from the batsman, Jeet lets it alone.
Full and outside off, Raval prods ahead and defends it into the ground.
Short of a length outside off, Raval stands inside his crease and defends it.
This was coming in! And so close to the off pole. Raval decides to leave it again but luckily for him, the ball doesn't come back enough.
Length ball, well outside off this time. The batsman chooses to leave it.
Overpitched and outside off, Raval drives it straight to mid off.
Good length ball on off, Latham pushes it to mid on and gets off the mark.
Shaheen Afridi to share the new ball.
Length ball outside off, Raval lets it go. Good start by Ali here.
Length delivery once again this time Raval blocks it away with a straight bat off his backfoot.
length delivery on middle and offs stump, the ball comes back in after pitching. Raval leaves it alone.
Length delivery outside off, Raval shoulders arms to it.
Full this time and Raval drives it through covers. The fielder dives and saves a certain boundary there.
Length delivery on the off stump, the ball moves away from the batsman after pitching. Raval lets it go.
